Both letters direct a department-level official to strengthen or establish an ongoing administrative program, explain how the program should operate, connect its work to reports to Congress, and conclude with an unusually close request for periodic progress reports to the President. C07 has a related program-strengthening structure and comparable emphasis on renewed, vigorous action, while C02 similarly transmits an advisory report and directs agency consideration, but neither matches the child's language and administrative sequence as closely as C24.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"From time to time, I hope you will report to me on the progress which is being made in the field of soldier voting.","parent_excerpt":"I hope that you will report to me from time to time on the progress of the agencies in carrying forward the historical program.","explanation":"This is a distinctive near-verbatim periodic-reporting formula, with only word order and the program subject adapted."},{"child_excerpt":"These recommendations appear to have merit, and I hope you will consider them carefully, and determine what steps may be appropriate to carry them out.","parent_excerpt":"For these reasons, I should like you to establish a Federal history program for all the agencies engaged in emergency activities. The active direction of the program should be undertaken by the Bureau of the Budget","explanation":"Both letters charge the recipient with implementing or developing an ongoing government-wide administrative program."},{"child_excerpt":"The Committee report further recommends that the Secretary of Defense gather and publish certain statistical data...","parent_excerpt":"These studies will also assist in the preparation of reports to the Congress.","explanation":"Both programs couple continuing agency information-gathering with formal reporting functions, reinforcing the structural parallel beyond the shared closing sentence."}]}
